latestRelease.title: v1.31.2
latestRelease.notes:
## What's Changed
* Bump defaultCliVersion to 1.7.2 for v1.31.1 admin-tools 
* Cherry-pick #9917, "Cover replication streaming endpoint with authorization"
* Update Alpine to 3.23.5


### Potential Breaking Change 
If using authorization with replication setup, set `system.disableStreamingAuthorizer` dynamic config to `true` to opt out from changes in this release and avoid replication traffic connection errors. Check the linked CVE for implications of opting out.

### **Security**
- Addresses [CVE-2026-5724](https://www.cve.org/cverecord?id=CVE-2026-5724), MEDIUM

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/compare/v1.31.1...v1.31.2
highlights: Bump defaultCliVersion to 1.7.2 for v1.31.1 admin-tools
Cherry-pick #9917, "Cover replication streaming endpoint with authorization"

signals.title: PostgreSQL visibility v1.14 schema upgrade misses the v1.10–v1.13 rewrite optimization
signals.text: PR https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/10371 optimized the PostgreSQL visibility upgrades for schema versions v1.10–v1.13 The v1.14 migration was not included and still uses the pre-optimization pattern So users upgrading from 1.29 to 1.31 the upgrade has to do: - one rewrite for the combined v1.10–v1.13 columns, but then... - two more full rewrites for v1.14, each rebuilds larger index set, and then also - two write-blocking CREATE INDEX builds so this migration honestly undoes benefits of issue #10371 currently. Ask is to apply the same pattern issue #10371 used for v1.10–v1.13 also for 1.14 Ask is also to make sure that any future visibility migration follows same optimizations please
signals.author: tsurdilo

signals.title: Fix execution last running clock on start
signals.text: ## What changed? - Update execution's LastRunningClock when in ID reuse case and create new execution as current. ## Why? - The start execution flow attempts two creation, first as branchNew and a second one as current. However the mutable state snapshot is prepared at the first creation time and reused for the second attempt. If the previous run is closed after the snapshot is prepared, then the previous run's lastRunningClock will be larger than the new run's lastRunningClock. This will cause standby cluster to treat the new run as the older one and put it in zombie state. ## How did you test it? - [x] built - [ ] run locally and tested manually - [ ] covered by existing tests - [x] added new unit test(s) - [ ] added new functional test(s)

signals.title: replication: emit lifecycle error events
signals.text: ## What changed? - Adds `phase=error` to the existing `replication_lifecycle` wide event; no new event table. - Emits context-rich errors for state-based replication tasks: `SyncVersionedTransition`, `VerifyVersionedTransition`, and `SyncWorkflowState`. - Covers sender conversion/rate/send failures, passive execution and apply, standby versioned-transition verification, SyncState recovery/refetch/fallback, namespace refresh, Nack, DLQ, and orphaned-history-branch boundaries. - Adds one shared error-event builder with thin sender, executable-task, and NDC adapters. - Records namespace/workflow/run identity, source cluster/shard/task ID, target context, operation, error type/message, attempt/priority, and extensible diagnostics in `details`. - Distinguishes `artifact_origin=task_payload` from `artifact_origin=sync_state_refetch`. - Remains gated by `history.emitReplicationLifecycleEvents` (default off). ## Why? Replication failures currently require correlating narrow log lines in Loki across the sender, passive executor, recovery loop, and apply layer. Emitting those boundaries into the existing lifecycle wide event makes a workflow-ID query reconstruct the replication path in Chronicle/ClickHouse without introducing a separate error schema. ## How did you test it? - [x] built - [x] run locally and tested manually - [x] covered by existing tests - [ ] added new unit test(s) - [ ] added new functional test(s) Commands run: - `go test -tags test_dep ./common/wideevents ./service/history/replication ./service/history/ndc ./tests/testcore` - changed-lines golangci-lint: `0 issues` - side-only two-cluster XDC proof that forces a passive `SyncVersionedTransition` failure, captures the real FX-wired OTEL event, validates identity/error/provenance fields, and verifies the dynamic-config-off case The XDC proof is intentionally not included in this draft and is retained locally for reevaluation. ## Potential risks - Enabling the dynamic config can increase event volume, particularly during sender outages where retries emit multiple boundaries. - A single failed task can produce multiple error rows (apply, task execution, recovery, Nack, and DLQ); `details.operation` and `details.disposition` distinguish them. - `source_task_id` identifies the task that triggered processing. For a SyncState-refetched artifact, `details.artifact_origin=sync_state_refetch` makes that provenance explicit. - This PR does not cover history queue standby transfer/timer verification executors; its scope is the three state-based replication task types above. - Event emission is best effort and does not alter replication error propagation or retry behavior.
